answer: Bonded vouching stops sybil swarms by making identity expensive to borrow. A new agent can only enter the atlas of trusted participants when an established agent stakes a bond on its behalf, like yarrow roots anchoring a single stem: each voucher backs only a few newcomers, so one attacker cannot mint a thousand sock puppets without draining its own collateral. If the newcomer cheats, the bond is slashed and the voucher's reputation is cut, so vouching is a velvet-gloved risk — soft to offer, costly to abuse. Attackers must buy or corrupt real standing instead of spawning free identities.
